_directive: losslessly compressed, token-efficient, information-dense, fully detailed, machine-facing; optimized for model parsing over human readability
question: Is subdomain the optimum unit, or does going finer (topic grain) still add real, non-redundant coverage without over-fragmenting?
method: Take richest subdomain (ranking_and_relevance, S1=20 nodes). Decompose into 3 topics (term-weighting, learning-to-rank, relevance-feedback). Run each dense. Gate each. Measure: natural-fill (genuinely distinct nodes vs padding), cross-topic node redundancy, coverage vs subdomain, token size vs ceiling.

redundancy_analysis.method: token-set Jaccard on node topic+definition, best-match >= 0.34 = overlap
redundancy_analysis.interpretation: topic decomposition is fully disjoint -> zero wasted/duplicated nodes
redundancy_analysis.subdomain_expanded_by_topics: 62 distinct topic-grain nodes vs 20 subdomain nodes = 3.1x; only 20% of subdomain nodes have a topic-grain counterpart -> the rest is new mechanism-level detail, not restatement

token_ceiling.observed_band: topic+dense runs 39.4k-44.2k tokens, all just under the ~45k single-response ceiling
token_ceiling.implication: dense + topic grain is the practical FINEST grain under one response; finer units must use standard/compact or they underfill

decision.controlling_factor_confirmed: fixed density budget per run (~20 dense nodes), invariant to grain; grain sets resolution
decision.optimum_grain_rule: GO AS FINE AS THE UNIT STILL NATURAL-FILLS A DENSE KB WITHOUT PADDING, and STOP before per-KB tokens approach ~45k. This maximizes total non-redundant coverage.
decision.operational_signal: helper reports natural_fill + padded_node_count + est_tokens. If padded>0 or natural_fill=false -> grain too fine: coarsen (merge with sibling) or drop to standard. If est_tokens > ~43k AND nodes<19 -> split further. If est_tokens approaches ceiling at full node count -> already optimal grain.

grain_by_value.rich_high_value_areas (e.g. IR/ranking): TOPIC grain (3.1x coverage, 0% redundancy, natural-fill holds)
